newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore, Indonesia to hold talks on development.
newsitem.headline: Singapore, Indonesia to hold talks on development.

text.p: Singapore's Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong will hold bilateral talks on regional development with Indonesia's President Suharto on Monday, a government statement said on Sunday.
Goh will visit Karimun, Indonesia to open the Karimun Marine & Industrial Complex (KIMC) and the PT Karimun Sembawang Shipyard (KSS) with President Suharto.
He will have a private meeting after that with President Suharto to exchange views on bilateral relations.
The KIMC project is part of the vision of both leaders to co-operate in the development of the island in the Riau Province.
The complex is the third industrial project developed under the Growth Triangle concept by private sectors of both countries.
KMIC is located 40 kilometres south-west of Singapore and is being developed by a group of Singapore and Indonesian companies.
It is expected to be completed in 10 years at an estimated total cost of Singapore $200 million.
PT KSS is situated in the north-western part of the island within the marine and industrial complex and is jointly developed by Sembawang Corp and Indonesia's Salim Group.
The first phase of development cost S$100 million, and plans are underway for the second phase costing an additional S$100 million.
